notes: Identity independently verified from the supplied canonical text: title Does Seeing Faces of Young Black Boys Facilitate the Identification of Threatening Stimuli?, authors Andrew R. Todd, Kelsey C. Thiem, and Rebecca Neel, Psychological Science 2016, 27(3), 384–393, DOI 10.1177/0956797615624492. This is a full primary research-article text, with methods, results and references, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied (source_pdf_path null), so no rendering was possible or performed. Only es_value_o is assigned; all other fields/sides are unassigned placeholders. The description identifies the safe-word error-rate simple effect across Black versus White primes, printed as gav = 0.23 with t(61) = 3.51 and p = .001 (exact bound). Requested partial eta-squared is not printed for this simple effect; no conversion performed. The nearby partial eta-squared .35 belongs to the Race of Prime × Target Word interaction, F(1, 61) = 32.30, p < .001, and is not the described simple effect. The opposite threatening-word error contrast is gav = 0.37 and is not the target. No N derivation performed.
